meta_description: Answers to the questions people ask Ayurvedachalam: what Ayurveda is, regulation, consultation cost, what to wear, insurance, herbs, and what we do not do.

data.lead: The questions people ask before they book, answered plainly. If yours is not here, the free 15-minute call is the fastest way to ask it.

faqs.a: The traditional medical system of India, several thousand years old, built around routine, food, oil therapies and herbs, and a way of describing constitution through three doshas. In Canada it is practised as a complementary tradition alongside, never instead of, medical care.

No province regulates it. There is no licence or register, so the practitioner's training is what you check. Ours is a five-and-a-half-year Indian university degree plus a hospital internship, evaluated by WES Canada; the Learn section has an article on exactly this.
Not in Canada. BAMS graduates practise as Ayurvedic physicians in India; here the degree is not a medical licence and we do not use the title "Dr."

faqs.q: What does a consultation cost, and how long is it?
faqs.a: $135 for 75 minutes, online or in person. Follow-ups are $75 for 30 minutes or $95 for 45. Prices are in Canadian dollars before GST.

faqs.q: Can you diagnose or treat my condition?
faqs.a: No. We do not diagnose, and we do not treat medical conditions. We help with routine, food, rest and traditional therapies, and we tell you when a question belongs to your physician.

Only when they fit, only products licensed by Health Canada with a Natural Product Number, and always with their cautions. We never recommend metal- or mineral-based preparations, and we do not sell products.

faqs.q: What should I wear to a therapy?
faqs.a: Whatever is comfortable; you undress as for a massage and are draped. Oil stays on the skin afterwards, so bring or wear clothes you do not mind a little oil on, and a hat in winter.

faqs.q: Is any of this covered by insurance?
faqs.a: Massage therapy by our RMT is receipted and usually covered up to your plan's maximum. Consultations, Shirodhara, Vasti and spiritual healing are not. The insurance page lists every service.
An external five-day program: Abhyanga, Shirodhara, Vasti, steam, diet and routine. No internal procedures; in Alberta those are restricted activities and we do not offer them.

faqs.q: Can I come if I am pregnant?
faqs.a: For a consultation, yes. Most therapies are not offered in the first trimester and are adapted afterwards with your physician's agreement. Each therapy page lists its own cautions.

faqs.q: Do you offer sessions in Tamil?
faqs.a: Yes. Consultations can be held in English or Tamil.
Online now, across Canada. The Calgary clinic opens soon; the address and hours will be published on the contact page.
